title: Verified dual-sourcing profit structure, optimal orders and reliability monotonicity
contribution_type: Four complete Lean formalizations of established dual-sourcing statements

owner.source_commit_scope: Completed owning-project publication record and lifecycle; source repository remains private. Exact accepted-proof source pin is also preserved in the archived packet.

claim: For the exact two-supplier random-capacity model: expected profit is lattice-submodular; a global maximizing feasible order exists with the necessary boundary-or-stationarity conclusion under absolutely continuous demand; the exact CDF derivative formula and its optimal-interior first-order consequence hold; and optimized expected profit is monotone in either supplier reliability for every nonnegative finite-mean demand law.

assumptions.suppliers: Two suppliers, indexed by Fin 2; positive finite design capacities.
assumptions.cost_parameters: 0 <= eta_i <= 1; r, p, c_i >= 0; v < r+p. These include disclosed platform additions.
assumptions.capacity_laws: For each reliability index, nonnegative atomless probability laws; CDF monotonicity in reliability is retained in Model.
assumptions.joint_law: The two capacity losses and demand are independent, through the exact product measure.
assumptions.feasible_orders: All componentwise nonnegative real vectors; no upper order cap is assumed.
assumptions.source_correspondence: The packet proves the complete platform signatures. The finite-mean and parameter qualifications supplied by the platform are disclosed; no equivalence to a broader unstated source theorem is claimed.
assumptions.demand_all_targets: A real probability law, nonnegative almost surely, with integrable identity.
assumptions.demand_theorem_1_and_equation_6: Absolute continuity with respect to Lebesgue measure. Lemmas 1 and 2(b) require no demand density.
assumptions.equation_6_only: Feasible orders, distinct supplier indices i,j and a strictly interior coordinate 0<q_i<K_i.
assumptions.reliability_lemma_2b: The full Model CDF-order assumption is retained. No derivative or smoothness of the reliability-indexed laws is added; the conclusion concerns the optimized value, not every fixed order.

limitations: Formalization of existing mathematics; no new mathematical discovery, exhaustive priority search, source-author endorsement or independent human review is claimed.
The complete platform model retains disclosed parameter and finite-mean assumptions. Kernel verification and source correspondence are distinct checks.
The appendix was consulted as extracted text but no immutable binary snapshot was obtained; proof equivalence to the appendix is not claimed.
The necessary first-order condition is not proved sufficient for optimality.

Region-by-region optimizer classification, optimal-quantity ordering and the wider mission remain separate obligations. Optimized-value monotonicity does not assert monotonicity of every fixed-order profit.
Verified third-party compiled caches remain trusted inputs; this is not a Lean/Mathlib bootstrap verification.
